books.name: Sparse 8×8, orthogonal
books.label: 8×8 orthogonal
books.blurb: Arrows point along rows and columns only, and there are few of them: 5 to 7 on a 8×8 board (one cell in 11 on average). Beginner to Hard.

books.name: Sparse 8×8, diagonal
books.label: 8×8 diagonal
books.blurb: Every arrow is diagonal, and there are few of them: 3 to 7 on a 8×8 board (one cell in 12 on average). Beginner to Hard.

books.name: Sparse 8×8, both
books.label: 8×8 both
books.blurb: Arrows point along rows, columns and diagonals, and there are few of them: 3 to 5 on a 8×8 board (one cell in 15 on average). Beginner to Hard.

books.name: Sparse 12×12, orthogonal
books.label: 12×12 orthogonal
books.blurb: Arrows point along rows and columns only, and there are few of them: 14 to 17 on a 12×12 board (one cell in 9 on average). Beginner to Hard.

books.name: Sparse 12×12, diagonal

books.name: Sparse 12×12, both
books.label: 12×12 both
books.blurb: Arrows point along rows, columns and diagonals, and there are few of them: 9 to 13 on a 12×12 board (one cell in 13 on average). Beginner to Hard.

books.name: Experiment: regional corpus
books.label: Regional corpus (experiment)
books.blurb: No arrows: thick lines cut the board into regions and a number says how many boxes its region holds. A spread of styles for finding the techniques.

books.name: Experiment: frame
books.label: Frame (experiment)
books.blurb: Arrows only round the border, pointing in; the rest of the border and some cells inside are void. Names show the recipe: L3 arrows on every third line with their real counts, U1 / U2 every arrow says 1 or 2, OR made with a constraint solver.
